findings.claim: The machine gate lives at harness/verify/checks.py, one directory beyond the literal touches ['server/','tests/']. Target 3 ('point the machine gate at the behavioral test') requires editing it, so it is in-scope per the mission BODY. NO server/ SOURCE was edited: the W5-LIFE owner (runtime_beat.py / session_store.py) is already genuine - W6-BEAT hardens the PROOF, not the owner. Bus-claimed the exact file+region and flagged the co-held checks.py seam to W6-PROV (region-disjoint by ~1400 lines).

On a full-package tree where the behavioural subprocess cannot import (genuine env failure), the gate keeps STRUCTURAL green with an honest INCONCLUSIVE note rather than RED - to avoid a flaky RED on environment problems. This is not a hole: the hollow-owner DEFECT is caught DETERMINISTICALLY via the sentinel (beaten_stays_healthy=False), because a hollow owner still imports fine and returns a sentinel; only a genuinely un-importable tree hits the inconclusive path, and that is disclosed, never faked green.

resilience.Watchdog is LAZY: it arms its monitor thread only on the FIRST heartbeat(), so a never-beaten chain never escalates. Both the gate proof and the behavioural tests MUST arm the chain with one direct beat before driving via the owner, else a hollow owner reads 'healthy' vacuously. Found first-hand this leg: the initial hollow simulation returned True (false-green) until the arming fix.
